pass_a_gloss: [...] God; your counsels drew near, says the king of Jacob. Having said very well how the calling of the nations will be in its times, and having promised to make the desert into marshes, and the thirsting land into watercourses, and to show it thick-haired with cedars and box and the other plants, and saying that his own hand will be marvelled at as craftsman of things so great, he speaks again to the makers of the idols and to the craftsmen of such things, and says that their judgment has come near. And judgment he calls either the punishment owed to them, or the shame and disgrace. For by a holy vote of God and by just judgment they would be punished as having deceived the [world] under heaven, and having brought in counsels not true. For they taught those on the earth to say to the wood: You are my father, and to the stone: You begot me. For this reason he says that their counsels drew near, that is, came to an end, God shaking down the error and scattering the mist from the ignorance, and not one of those among them, of the falsely named ones clearly we say, but the Lord and God in truth, and the king of Jacob, that is, of those from the blood of Israel. And he brings through these things into remembrance of the signs that happened at the redemption of those from Israel, through which very well is recognized the power of the authority befitting God that is in him, or of the incomparable pre-eminence. [Lemma, Isaiah 41:22-24:] Let them draw near, and let them announce to you what will happen, or the former things, what they were; say, and we will set the mind on [it], and we will know what the last things are and the things coming upon. Tell us, announce the things coming upon at the last, and we will know that you are gods. Do good, and do evil, and we will marvel, and we will see together; for from where are you, and from where your work? From earth they chose you an abomination. It is proper and exceptional to the divine and ineffable glory to know all things, and to be ignorant of wholly nothing, neither of the things that happened before, nor of the things present, or of those that will be. And indeed through [another reading: through] the all-wise Moses he makes the things before the framing of this world, and the things in beginnings, clear to those on the earth, saying: In beginning God made the heaven and the earth. And the earth was invisible and unconstructed, and darkness above the abyss; and he goes through most exactly the making of the whole world. But also our Lord Jesus Christ, who spoke of old those things through Moses, announced to us the things at the last; for as his disciple says: New heavens and a new earth and his promises we await. And it is possible to hear him saying clearly: Will anything be hidden from me? And: For truly living is the word of God, and clear, and [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … God; “your counsels have drawn near,” says the King of Jacob (Isaiah 41:21).

He has declared very clearly how the calling of the nations will come about in its due time; He has promised to turn the desert into marshes and the thirsty land into watercourses, and to make it thick with cedars and box trees and other plants (Isaiah 41:18-19); and He has said that His own hand will be marvelled at as the Maker of such great things (Isaiah 41:20). Now He speaks again to the makers of idols and to the craftsmen of such things, and says that their judgment has come near. By judgment He means the punishment owed to them, that is, their shame and disgrace. For by the holy sentence of God and by a just judgment they would be punished, as men who have deceived the whole world under heaven and brought in counsels that are not true. For they taught those on earth to say to the wood, “You are my father,” and to the stone, “You begot me” (Jeremiah 2:27).

That is why He says that their counsels have drawn near, that is, have come to their end, since God is shaking down the error and scattering the mist of ignorance: not one of the gods they have, those falsely so called, we mean, but the Lord, God in truth, and the King of Jacob, that is, of those of the blood of Israel. By these words He brings to remembrance the signs that took place at the redemption of those of Israel, through which the power of the authority befitting God that is in Him, or of His incomparable pre-eminence, is very clearly recognised.

“Let them draw near and declare to you what will happen; or what the former things were, tell us, and we will set our mind on it, and we will know what the last things are and the things to come. Tell us, declare the things that are coming at the last, and we will know that you are gods. Do good, and do harm, and we will marvel and see together; for where are you from, and where is your work from? From the earth they chose you, an abomination” (Isaiah 41:22-24).

It is the proper and singular mark of the divine and ineffable glory to know all things and to be wholly ignorant of nothing, whether of what has happened before, or of what is present, or of what will be. Indeed, through the all-wise Moses He makes plain to those on earth the things before the framing of this world and the things at the beginning, saying: “In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. And the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss” (Genesis 1:1-2); and He goes through the making of the whole world most exactly.

But our Lord Jesus Christ too, who spoke those things of old through Moses, has declared to us the things at the end; for, as His disciple says, “We look for new heavens and a new earth, and His promises” (2 Peter 3:13). And one may hear Him saying plainly: “Will anything be hidden from Me?” (Jeremiah 32:27); and: “For the word of God is truly living, and clear, and …” (Hebrews 4:12).

choices.why: The King of Jacob speaks Isaiah 41:21 against the idolaters; he does not affirm their counsels.
rejected: the King of Jacob affirms the idolaters' counsels
